UADataType.Description: Fine-grained execution state of an intent or a mission. This REFINES the Part 10 program state machine rather than restating it: Queued, Cancelling and the three terminal outcomes cannot be told apart from CurrentState alone. Clause 6.3 fixes which ExecutionState may accompany which Part 10 state, and a Server shall satisfy that table.

Field.Name: Accepted
Field.Description: Admitted and validated, not yet queued or executing.

Field.Name: Queued
Field.Description: Waiting behind another intent because BufferMode is Buffered or a blending mode. Corresponds to PLCopen Busy without Active.

Field.Name: Executing
Field.Description: Commanding the robot now.

Field.Name: Suspended
Field.Description: Paused by request; position is retained and execution can resume.

Field.Name: Cancelling
Field.Description: A cancel was accepted and the Server is bringing the motion to a controlled end. Not yet terminal.

Field.Name: Succeeded
Field.Description: Terminal. Completed as requested.

Field.Name: Failed
Field.Description: Terminal. Did not complete; Failure carries the reason.

Field.Name: Cancelled
Field.Description: Terminal. Ended early because a cancel was accepted.

Field.Name: Retriable
Field.Description: Terminal for now, but the Server can re-attempt it on Retry. A Server that does not offer Retry never enters this state and reports Failed instead.

UADataType.Description: How a newly submitted intent relates to the one already executing. The values and their meanings are those of PLCopen Motion Control MC_BufferMode, adopted unchanged because every motion runtime already implements them. In all blending modes the robot does not decelerate to a stop at the boundary, and the predecessor reaches Succeeded when blending begins rather than when its target is exactly attained.

Field.Name: Aborting
Field.Description: Abort what is executing and start immediately. The aborted intent terminates as Cancelled. This is the default.

Field.Name: Buffered
Field.Description: Queue; start when the predecessor succeeds.

Field.Name: BlendingLow
Field.Description: Blend at the lower of the two boundary speeds.

Field.Name: BlendingPrevious
Field.Description: Blend at the predecessor's boundary speed.

Field.Name: BlendingNext
Field.Description: Blend at the successor's boundary speed.

Field.Name: BlendingHigh
Field.Description: Blend at the higher of the two boundary speeds.

UADataType.Description: Whether an intent tolerates motion and other intents running alongside it. The four values are the two-by-two matrix of VDA 5050 blockingType, adopted because it is the only widely deployed concurrency annotation for robot actions.

Field.Name: None
Field.Description: Runs in the background; motion may continue and other intents may run concurrently.

Field.Name: Soft
Field.Description: Motion stops for the duration; other intents may still run.

Field.Name: Single
Field.Description: Motion may continue; no other intent may run concurrently.

Field.Name: Hard
Field.Description: Motion stops and no other intent may run concurrently. The intent has exclusive use of the robot.

UADataType.Description: Whether a motion ends exactly on its target or is blended into the next one. This is the only distinction every vendor expresses identically; the blend magnitude in BlendDataType.Radius is a request, not a guarantee.

Field.Name: Exact
Field.Description: Come to rest on the target before the next motion begins. ABB fine, FANUC FINE, Yaskawa PL=0, KUKA no approximation.

Field.Name: Blend
Field.Description: Round the corner into the next motion without stopping.

UADataType.Description: How a held object is given up.

Field.Name: Drop
Field.Description: Open the end effector where it is, without placing.

Field.Name: Place
Field.Description: Set the object down under control at the target.

Field.Name: Handover
Field.Description: Retain the object until the Server judges a receiving party has taken it.

UADataType.Description: Direction from which an end effector approaches an object or a placement.

Field.Name: Default
Field.Description: The Server chooses.

Field.Name: ToolZ
Field.Description: Along the tool's own Z axis.

Field.Name: Top
Field.Description: From above, in the frame the target is expressed in.

Field.Name: Side
Field.Description: Laterally, in the frame the target is expressed in.

UADataType.Description: Role of a coordinate frame, following the coordinate systems ISO 9787 standardises. The roles say WHICH frames exist; no standard says how to calibrate between them, which is why CoordinateFrameType carries the transform explicitly.

Field.Name: World
Field.Description: The cell-level reference frame.

Field.Name: Base
Field.Description: The robot base frame.

Field.Name: MechanicalInterface
Field.Description: The flange at the end of the last link, to which an end effector is fitted.

Field.Name: Tool
Field.Description: A tool frame, whose origin is a tool centre point.

Field.Name: Object
Field.Description: A workpiece or work-object frame.

Field.Name: Other
Field.Description: A frame whose role is none of the above.

UADataType.Description: Operational mode of the robot system, as defined by ISO 10218-1 and reported identically by OPC 40010-1. It is READ-ONLY here: mode selection is a safety function performed by safety-rated means, and this specification defines no way to command it. Clause 10 restricts intent submission to Automatic and AutomaticExternal.

Field.Name: Other
Field.Description: Booting, uncalibrated, or a safety system fault.

Field.Name: ManualReducedSpeed
Field.Description: Teaching mode with a speed ceiling and a held enabling device.

Field.Name: ManualHighSpeed
Field.Description: Program verification with an enabling device.

Field.Name: Automatic
Field.Description: Automatic operation with the safeguarded space secured.

Field.Name: AutomaticExternal
Field.Description: Automatic operation commanded by an external system. This is the mode this specification is written for.

UADataType.Description: Why an intent did not succeed. The set is deliberately small and diagnosable: a client decides whether to retry, re-plan or escalate from this value alone, and reads Message only to show a human.

Field.Name: None
Field.Description: No failure. Reported on a successful outcome.

Field.Name: Unreachable
Field.Description: The target lies outside the reachable workspace.

Field.Name: Kinematics
Field.Description: No kinematic solution, or a singularity on the path.

Field.Name: Collision
Field.Description: A collision was predicted or detected.

Field.Name: JointLimit
Field.Description: A joint limit would be or was exceeded.

Field.Name: SpeedLimit
Field.Description: The requested speed or acceleration is not permitted in the active mode.

Field.Name: ToolMissing
Field.Description: The required tool is not fitted or not identified.

Field.Name: ObjectNotFound
Field.Description: The object to act on was not present.

Field.Name: GraspFailed
Field.Description: The object was not acquired, or was lost in transit.

Field.Name: Timeout
Field.Description: The intent did not complete within its permitted time.

Field.Name: NotPermittedInMode
Field.Description: Refused because the operational mode does not permit it. See clause 10.

Field.Name: ControlNotOwned
Field.Description: Refused because the caller does not hold command authority. See clause 8.

Field.Name: CapabilityNotSupported
Field.Description: The Server does not implement this intent type, or this combination of options.

Field.Name: ParameterInvalid
Field.Description: A parameter was missing, malformed or out of range.

Field.Name: QueueFull
Field.Description: The queue is at MaxQueueDepth.

Field.Name: Superseded
Field.Description: An Aborting submission or a mission update replaced it before it could run.

Field.Name: HardwareFault
Field.Description: A fault in the robot, the end effector or the controller.

Field.Name: SafetyStop
Field.Description: A safety function acted. The safety system, not this interface, decided this.

Field.Name: Other
Field.Description: A reason none of the above describes; see Message.

Field.Name: SafetyLimitExceeded
Field.Description: Refused because the request would exceed a limit the safety system is enforcing. See clause 10.3.

UADataType.Description: How urgently a cancellation should bring motion to an end. The values are those of PossibleStopModes in OPC 40010-1, so a Server implementing both reports one vocabulary. This is an APPLICATION-LEVEL request: it does not select, imply or guarantee any IEC 60204-1 stop category, which only the robot's safety system determines. See clause 10.

Field.Name: OnPath
Field.Description: Decelerate along the programmed path.

Field.Name: EndOfCycle
Field.Description: Stop when the current cycle completes.

Field.Name: ProcessStop
Field.Description: Stop at a point the process defines as safe.

Field.Name: QuickStop
Field.Description: Decelerate as quickly as the drives allow.

Field.Name: EndOfInstruction
Field.Description: Stop when the current instruction completes.

UADataType.Description: Whether an axis rotates or translates. This fixes the unit of the corresponding entry of JointMoveIntentDataType.JointTargets.

Field.Name: Revolute
Field.Description: Rotates. Its joint target is in radians.

Field.Name: Prismatic
Field.Description: Translates. Its joint target is in metres.

UADataType.Description: Outcome of a mission update, reported so a client can tell a stale update from a rejected one without parsing a StatusCode.

Field.Name: Accepted
Field.Description: The horizon was replaced as requested.

Field.Name: Outdated
Field.Description: MissionUpdateId was not greater than the current one.

Field.Name: BaseConflict
Field.Description: The update would have altered a released step.

Field.Name: UnknownMission
Field.Description: No mission with that MissionId is held.

Field.Name: Rejected
Field.Description: Refused for a reason the Server states in a message.

UADataType.Description: A rigid-body pose. Position is metres; Orientation is a UNIT QUATERNION ordered (x, y, z, w). Quaternions are used because OPC UA defines no quaternion type and the Euler triple in ThreeDOrientation is ambiguous without an external convention; Annex C gives the normative conversion to and from ThreeDFrame. All frames are right-handed. FrameId names the CoordinateFrame the pose is expressed in; an empty FrameId means the Server's default work frame.

Field.Name: FrameId
Field.Description: FrameId of the CoordinateFrame this pose is expressed in; empty for the default work frame.

Field.Name: Position
Field.Description: Translation (x, y, z) in metres.

Field.Name: Orientation
Field.Description: Unit quaternion (x, y, z, w).

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Limits a motion is to respect. Every field is a REQUEST bounded by what the robot is configured to permit: a Server clamps rather than refuses, except where clause 10 requires refusal. A value of zero or less means the field is unspecified and the Server chooses.

Field.Name: SpeedFraction
Field.Description: Fraction of the configured maximum speed, in the range 0 to 1. This is the portable speed control: every vendor supports it.

Field.Name: CartesianSpeed
Field.Description: Tool centre point speed in metres per second. Ignored by joint moves.

Field.Name: CartesianAcceleration
Field.Description: Tool centre point acceleration in metres per second squared.

Field.Name: Jerk
Field.Description: Rate of change of acceleration in metres per second cubed.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: How a motion ends. Radius is interpreted only when Termination is Blend, and is a request: controllers that expose a unitless blend scale rather than a distance map it as best they can, and a Server that cannot honour the exact radius still succeeds.

Field.Name: Termination
Field.Description: Exact stop, or blend into the next motion.

Field.Name: Radius
Field.Description: Blend radius in metres, measured from the target. Zero or less means the Server chooses.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Abstract base of every intent. An intent is a single task-level request; it is what a client submits and what a mission step holds, so the two are the same shape. Extension is by SUBTYPING this structure, which keeps new intents discoverable through IntentCapabilitiesType rather than by probing for BrowseNames.

Field.Name: IntentId
Field.Description: Client-assigned identifier, unique among the intents the client has outstanding. Empty asks the Server to assign one, which it returns.

Field.Name: Label
Field.Description: Human-readable description. Never interpreted.

Field.Name: BufferMode
Field.Description: How this intent relates to one already executing.

Field.Name: BlockingMode
Field.Description: Whether motion and other intents may proceed alongside it.

UADataType.Description: Abstract base of the intents that move the robot. ToolFrame names the frame whose origin is driven to the target - without it a pose target is meaningless, and OPC 40010-1 defines no tool centre point at all.

Field.Name: ToolFrame
Field.Description: The CoordinateFrame, of role Tool, whose origin is driven to the target. Null means the tool currently fitted.

Field.Name: Constraints
Field.Description: Speed and acceleration limits for this motion.

Field.Name: Blend
Field.Description: How this motion ends.

UADataType.Description: Move by interpolating in joint space. This is the fastest way between two configurations and the path the tool centre point takes is not controlled. It is the portable equivalent of PTP, MoveJ, J and MOVJ. Giving a pose rather than joint values asks the Server to solve the kinematics itself, which is the 'move to this pose, you choose how' case.

Field.Name: HasJointTargets
Field.Description: True when JointTargets is meaningful; False when TargetPose is.

Field.Name: JointTargets
Field.Description: One value per axis, in the order the axes are declared under the controller: radians for a Revolute axis, metres for a Prismatic one.

Field.Name: TargetPose
Field.Description: Pose to reach, used when HasJointTargets is False.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Move the tool centre point along a straight line to the target. The portable equivalent of LIN, MoveL, L and MOVL.

Field.Name: Target
Field.Description: Pose to reach.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Move the tool centre point along the circular arc that passes through ViaPoint and ends at Target. The portable equivalent of CIRC, MoveC, C and MOVC. Only the position of ViaPoint defines the arc; its orientation is ignored.

Field.Name: ViaPoint
Field.Description: A pose on the arc between the start and the target. Only its position is used.

Field.Name: Target
Field.Description: Pose to reach.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Close the end effector on an object. Force and Width are requests; an end effector that cannot regulate force ignores Force and still succeeds.

Field.Name: Tool
Field.Description: The Tool to actuate. Null means the tool currently fitted.

Field.Name: Force
Field.Description: Grasp force in newtons. Zero or less means the Server chooses.

Field.Name: Width
Field.Description: Opening at which to close, in metres. Zero or less means the Server chooses.

Field.Name: Approach
Field.Description: Direction of approach.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Give up a held object.

Field.Name: Tool
Field.Description: The Tool to actuate. Null means the tool currently fitted.

Field.Name: Mode
Field.Description: How the object is given up.

Field.Name: HasTarget
Field.Description: True when Target is meaningful.

Field.Name: Target
Field.Description: Where to place the object, when Mode is Place.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Take an object from a location. Source is a REFERENCE TO A LOCATION NODE, not a name: the location's pose and its properties are then read from the address space, so the station identity has exactly one definition.

Field.Name: Source
Field.Description: The Location to pick from.

Field.Name: Tool
Field.Description: The Tool to use. Null means the tool currently fitted.

Field.Name: ObjectClass
Field.Description: What to pick, when the location can hold more than one kind. Empty means whatever is there.

Field.Name: Force
Field.Description: Grasp force in newtons. Zero or less means the Server chooses.

Field.Name: Approach
Field.Description: Direction of approach.

Field.Name: Attributes
Field.Description: Further named parameters the Server declares in its capabilities.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Put a held object at a location. Destination is a reference to a Location node, for the same reason as PickIntentDataType.Source.

Field.Name: Destination
Field.Description: The Location to place at.

Field.Name: Tool
Field.Description: The Tool to use. Null means the tool currently fitted.

Field.Name: Approach
Field.Description: Direction of approach.

Field.Name: Attributes
Field.Description: Further named parameters the Server declares in its capabilities.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Exchange the fitted end effector.

Field.Name: Tool
Field.Description: The Tool to fit. Null means release the fitted tool and fit nothing.

Field.Name: DockStation
Field.Description: The Location of the tool changer. Null lets the Server choose.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Set a discrete or analogue output. Output references an OutputSignal node, so the signal's meaning, range and unit are described once in the address space instead of being implied by a string.

Field.Name: Output
Field.Description: The OutputSignal to write.

Field.Name: Value
Field.Description: Value to write, of the signal's own DataType.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Run a program that already exists on the controller. This is the escape hatch for capability this specification does not model, and the bridge to the OPC 40010-1 task control surface.

Field.Name: Program
Field.Description: The Program to run.

Field.Name: Arguments
Field.Description: Named arguments for the program.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Do nothing for a while, or until released. A mission needs this to express a rendezvous with something the robot does not control; without it a client has to hold the queue open from outside.

Field.Name: Duration
Field.Description: How long to wait, in milliseconds. Zero or less waits until Signal is released.

Field.Name: Signal
Field.Description: An OutputSignal under this controller, or another Variable of DataType Boolean, whose becoming true ends the wait. Null waits only for Duration. Clause 11.3 requires the Server to check that it resolves to one of those two, under the controller being commanded, and to refuse it otherwise.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: The outcome of one intent, preserved after it terminates. AchievedPose records where the tool centre point actually ended, which is what lets a client tell a blended corner from an exact stop and audit a placement.

Field.Name: IntentId
Field.Description: The intent this describes.

Field.Name: State
Field.Description: Terminal state reached.

Field.Name: Failure
Field.Description: Reason, or None on success.

Field.Name: Message
Field.Description: Human-readable detail. Never parsed.

Field.Name: HasAchievedPose
Field.Description: True when AchievedPose is meaningful.

Field.Name: AchievedPose
Field.Description: Where the tool centre point came to rest, or was when blending began.

Field.Name: StartTime
Field.Description: When execution began.

Field.Name: EndTime
Field.Description: When the terminal state was reached.

Field.Name: Outputs
Field.Description: Named results the intent produced, for example the identity of a picked object.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: One step of a mission. Released is what splits a mission into its immutable base and its revisable horizon: a released step has been committed and may already be executing, so an update may not touch it. Status is a HINT - where Operation is not null, that IntentOperation's state machine decides.

Field.Name: StepId
Field.Description: Identifier unique within the mission.

Field.Name: SequenceId
Field.Description: Execution order within the mission, ascending.

Field.Name: Released
Field.Description: True for a base step, which is committed and immutable. False for a horizon step, which an update may replace or remove.

Field.Name: Intent
Field.Description: The intent this step executes.

Field.Name: Status
Field.Description: Reported status. Where Operation is not null its state machine is authoritative and this reflects it.

Field.Name: Operation
Field.Description: The IntentOperation executing this step, or null while the step has not begun.

Field.Name: ErrorPolicy
Field.Description: What the mission does when this step does not succeed.

Field.Name: FallbackStepId
Field.Description: The step to continue at, when ErrorPolicy is Fallback or Compensate.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: An ordered sequence of intents submitted and tracked as a unit. MissionUpdateId increases with every update, so a Server can reject an update that crossed with another in flight instead of applying it out of order.

Field.Name: MissionId
Field.Description: Client-assigned identifier. Empty asks the Server to assign one, which it returns.

Field.Name: MissionUpdateId
Field.Description: Revision of this mission, increasing. The first submission is 0.

Field.Name: Label
Field.Description: Human-readable description. Never interpreted.

Field.Name: Steps
Field.Description: The steps, in ascending SequenceId order.

Field.Name: Transitions
Field.Description: The step graph. An empty array means the steps run in order, which is the flat sequence a mission without branching has always been.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: What the Server will accept for one intent type. This is the machine-readable declaration that makes an intent surface discoverable: a client reads it once and knows what it may submit, instead of submitting to find out. It is the analogue of the VDA 5050 factsheet.

Field.Name: IntentType
Field.Description: The DataType of the intent, a subtype of IntentDataType.

Field.Name: Description
Field.Description: What this Server does with it.

Field.Name: CancelSupported
Field.Description: True when Cancel is honoured for it. A Server may still refuse a particular cancel; see clause 6.5.

Field.Name: PauseSupported
Field.Description: True when Pause and Resume are honoured for a running intent. False when the Server can only stop its queue: suspending execution means the robot stops, and Suspended is never reported while it is still moving.

Field.Name: RetrySupported
Field.Description: True when it can terminate Retriable and be re-attempted.

Field.Name: SupportedBufferModes
Field.Description: Buffer modes accepted for it. Aborting is always accepted and always listed.

Field.Name: SupportedBlockingModes
Field.Description: Blocking modes accepted for it.

Field.Name: Attributes
Field.Description: Named parameters this Server recognises in the intent's Attributes field.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UAReferenceType.Description: Binds an intent surface to the thing it commands. This is how the model attaches to a robot described by another specification - an OPC 40010-1 MotionDeviceSystem, say - without depending on it. Annex B defines that binding.

From a CoordinateFrame to the frame its Transform is expressed in. Frames form a tree, so a pose given in one frame can be re-expressed in another by composing the transforms along the path between them.

UAObjectType.Description: Server-level entry point. A client that has just connected browses here to find every robot it can command, without knowing the Server's layout.

UAObject.Description: The intent surfaces this Server offers, one per commandable robot.

UAVariable.Description: Release of this specification the Server implements, for example '0.1.0'.

UAObjectType.Description: The intent surface for one robot: what it can be asked to do, the frames and objects those requests refer to, and the intents and missions currently outstanding. Everything a client needs in order to command the robot hangs from here.

UAVariable.Description: Operational mode reported by the robot. Read-only: mode selection is a safety function and this specification defines no way to command it. Clause 10 restricts submission to Automatic and AutomaticExternal.
True when the robot will accept intents now. A client checks this before submitting rather than inferring readiness from OperationalMode alone.
SessionId of the client that currently holds command authority, or null when no client does. Only that client may submit; see clause 8.
How many intents may be queued behind the executing one. Zero means the Server accepts only Aborting submissions.
The IntentOperation executing now, or null.
The Mission executing now, or null.

UAObject.Description: What this robot will accept.
The coordinate frames poses may be expressed in.
The end effectors this robot can use.
The named places intents refer to.
The axes, in the order JointMoveIntentDataType.JointTargets uses.
The signals SetOutput can write.
The controller programs CallProgram can run.
Outstanding and recently completed intents, one Object each.
Outstanding and recently completed missions, one Object each.

UAMethod.Description: Take command authority. A Server grants it only when no other Session holds it, or when the holder's Session has closed. Holding authority is a precondition for submitting, and exists so that two clients cannot interleave motion; it is NOT the single point of control that ISO 10218-2 requires, which is enforced by safety-rated means outside this interface.

uax:Description.uax:Text: True when the caller now holds authority.
SessionId of the holder after the call.

UAMethod.Description: Give up command authority. Outstanding intents are unaffected; use CancelAll to stop them.

Submit one intent. Returns as soon as the intent is admitted - NOT when the robot has finished, which may be minutes later. The returned Operation is a node the client subscribes to for progress and reads for the result. This is the whole reason the model is built on the Part 10 program lifecycle: an OPC UA Call cannot stay open for the duration of a motion.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The intent to execute.
True when the intent was admitted. False is a refusal, which clause 10.5 makes an ordinary outcome rather than an error.
Identifier of the intent, assigned by the Server when the request left it empty. Empty on a refusal.
The IntentOperation that tracks it. Null on a refusal, because a refusal creates no operation instance.
Why the intent was refused, or None when it was admitted.
Human-readable detail on a refusal. For a human; never parsed.

UAMethod.Description: Ask the Server to end an intent early. The Server MAY refuse, and says so in Accepted, because some motions cannot be abandoned safely part-way. This is not the OPC UA Cancel Service, which discards a pending response and leaves the robot moving; see clause 6.5.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The intent to cancel.
How urgently to stop.
True when the Server will act on it.

UAMethod.Description: Ask the Server to end every outstanding intent and mission.

uax:Description.uax:Text: How urgently to stop.
How many were acted on.

UAMethod.Description: Suspend execution, retaining position so it can be resumed.

uax:Description.uax:Text: True when execution is suspending.
True when execution is resuming.

UAMethod.Description: Re-attempt an intent that terminated Retriable.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The intent to re-attempt.
True when a new attempt was admitted.
The IntentOperation that tracks the new attempt. Null on a refusal.
Why the re-attempt was refused, or None when it was admitted.
Human-readable detail on a refusal.

UAMethod.Description: Submit an ordered sequence of intents as one unit. Steps marked Released form the base and are committed; the rest form the horizon and may still be revised by UpdateMission.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The mission to execute.
True when the mission was admitted.
Identifier of the mission, assigned by the Server when the request left it empty. Empty on a refusal.
The Mission that tracks it. Null on a refusal.
Why the mission was refused, or None when it was admitted.
Human-readable detail on a refusal.

UAMethod.Description: Replace the horizon of a mission already submitted. The base is untouchable: it has been committed and may already have executed, so an update that would alter a released step is refused rather than partly applied.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The mission to update.
Revision of the update. Must be greater than the mission's current value.
The steps that replace the horizon.
Outcome of the update.
Human-readable detail on a refusal.

UAMethod.Description: Ask the Server to end a mission and every intent belonging to it.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The mission to cancel.
How urgently to stop.
True when the Server will act on it.

UAObjectType.Description: One submitted intent, tracked to completion. It is a Part 10 program instance, so its lifecycle is the one OPC UA already defines for work that outlives a service call: transitions raise ProgramTransitionEvents, the terminal result survives in FinalResultData, and ProgramDiagnostic2DataType records which Session commanded it without this specification having to model provenance itself.

UAVariable.Description: Identifier of the intent this instance executes.
The intent as admitted, after the Server applied its defaults. A client reads this to learn what it actually asked for.
Fine-grained state. It refines CurrentState rather than restating it; clause 6.3 fixes which pairs are legal.
Fraction of the intent completed, 0 to 1, where the Server can estimate it. Negative means it cannot.

Where the driven tool centre point is now. Subscribe for tracking; this is a status report at the sampling rate the client asks for, not a control signal, and clause 4.3 explains why it must not be used as one.
Outcome, meaningful once ExecutionState is terminal. The same value is placed under FinalResultData so a Part 10 client finds it where Part 10 says it will be.
The mission this intent belongs to, or empty when it was submitted alone.
Place in the queue while ExecutionState is Queued, 1 being next. Zero once it is no longer queued.

UAObjectType.Description: One submitted mission, tracked to completion. It is a Part 10 program instance for the same reasons an IntentOperation is, and it owns the IntentOperations of its steps.

UAVariable.Description: Identifier of the mission this instance executes.
Revision currently in force.
The mission as it now stands, base and horizon together.
Fine-grained state, refining CurrentState as clause 6.3 fixes.
The step executing now, or empty.
How many steps are in the base. The first this many steps of Mission.Steps are committed; the rest are the horizon.

UAObjectType.Description: What one robot will accept. A client reads this once, before it submits anything, and knows what the robot can do and under what constraints.

UAVariable.Description: One entry per intent type this Server accepts.
True when SubmitMission is implemented.
True when UpdateMission can revise the horizon of a running mission.
True when the blending buffer modes actually blend. A Server that treats them as Buffered reports False, so a client is not misled about the path.
Largest blend radius the robot will honour, in metres. Zero or less means it is not bounded here.
How many axes JointMoveIntentDataType.JointTargets must carry.

UAObjectType.Description: A named right-handed Cartesian frame. Frames form a tree through HasFrameParent, so a client can compose a chain from a tool frame to a world frame. Roles follow ISO 9787, which standardises which frames exist; the transform between them is carried explicitly because no standard says how to calibrate it.

UAVariable.Description: Identifier referenced by Pose3DDataType.FrameId. Unique among the frames of one controller.
Role of this frame.
Pose of this frame within its parent. Ignored for a root frame.

UAObjectType.Description: An end effector. Its tool centre point is a CoordinateFrame of role Tool, which is what a motion intent drives to a target - OPC 40010-1 models robot topology in detail but has no tool centre point at all, so this specification supplies one.

UAVariable.Description: Identifier unique within the controller.
Human-readable name.
True when this tool is on the robot now.
The CoordinateFrame, of role Tool, that is this tool's centre point.
Mass in kilograms. Zero or less when not stated.
Largest grasp force in newtons, or zero when the tool does not grasp.
Largest opening in metres, or zero when the tool does not grasp.

UAObjectType.Description: A named place an intent can refer to. Pick and Place reference these nodes rather than naming a station in a string, so a location has one definition that a client can read, subscribe to and reason about.

UAVariable.Description: Identifier unique within the controller.
Human-readable name.
Where the location is.
True when the Server believes something is there.
What the location holds, when it holds one kind of thing. Empty otherwise.
How many objects it can hold. Zero means unstated.

UAObjectType.Description: One axis of the robot. The order of these nodes under the controller's Axes folder fixes the order of JointMoveIntentDataType.JointTargets, and Kind fixes each entry's unit.

UAVariable.Description: Identifier unique within the controller.
Position in JointTargets, counting from zero.
Whether it rotates or translates, which fixes the unit of its joint target.
Lower limit, in radians or metres by Kind.
Upper limit, in radians or metres by Kind.
Largest speed, in radians or metres per second by Kind.
Where the axis is now, in radians or metres by Kind.

UAObjectType.Description: A signal SetOutput can write. Modelling it as a node means the range, the unit and the meaning are described once, instead of every client having to know what a line name implies.

UAVariable.Description: Identifier unique within the controller.
Human-readable name.
Current value.
True when SetOutput may write it.
Unit of an analogue signal.

UAObjectType.Description: A program held on the controller that CallProgram can run. This is the bridge to capability this specification does not model, and to the programs an OPC 40010-1 task control already exposes.

UAVariable.Description: Identifier unique within the controller.
Human-readable name.
What the program does.
Named parameters it accepts, with their default values.

UAObject.Description: Entry point for robot intent on this Server. A client browses Server/RobotIntent/Controllers to find every robot it can command.

UADataType.Description: The safe motion function a safety system is enforcing, as defined by IEC 61800-5-2. This is a REPORT. The safety system enforces these independently of this interface, and a client reading them has not thereby obtained any safety function - see clause 10.

Field.Name: None
Field.Description: No safe motion function is active.

Field.Name: Sto
Field.Description: Safe Torque Off: torque is removed.

Field.Name: Ss1
Field.Description: Safe Stop 1: a controlled ramp to standstill, then Safe Torque Off.

Field.Name: Ss2
Field.Description: Safe Stop 2: a controlled ramp to standstill, which is then held under power.

Field.Name: Sos
Field.Description: Safe Operating Stop: standstill is monitored while the drive remains energised.

Field.Name: Sls
Field.Description: Safely Limited Speed: speed is monitored against a limit.

Field.Name: Slp
Field.Description: Safely Limited Position: position is monitored against a limit.

Field.Name: Sdi
Field.Description: Safe Direction: motion is permitted in one direction only.

Field.Name: Sbc
Field.Description: Safe Brake Control: a brake is commanded safely.

UADataType.Description: The transport of a brokered real-time channel. This specification defines none of these: it describes them so a client can find and open one, and the samples never traverse this interface.

Field.Name: Rtde
Field.Description: Universal Robots Real-Time Data Exchange.

Field.Name: Egm
Field.Description: ABB Externally Guided Motion.

Field.Name: Fri
Field.Description: KUKA Fast Research Interface.

Field.Name: Rsi
Field.Description: KUKA Robot Sensor Interface.

Field.Name: MotoRos2
Field.Description: Yaskawa MotoROS2.

Field.Name: OpcUaFx
Field.Description: OPC UA FX (OPC 10000-80 to -84). The open path, and the only one in this list that is an OPC Foundation specification.

Field.Name: Other
Field.Description: A transport identified by the channel's own descriptor.

UADataType.Description: Which end opens the transport connection of a brokered channel. Getting this wrong is the usual reason a first connection attempt fails, so it is stated rather than left to the reader.

Field.Name: Server
Field.Description: The Server connects to an endpoint the client is listening on.

Field.Name: Client
Field.Description: The client connects to the endpoint the Server publishes.

UADataType.Description: What a mission does when one of its steps does not succeed. Without this a mission can only abort, which forces every recovery out into the client.

Field.Name: Abort
Field.Description: End the mission. This is the default and the behaviour of a mission that declares no policy.

Field.Name: Retry
Field.Description: Re-attempt the step. A Server bounds the attempts and reports Failed when they are exhausted.

Field.Name: Skip
Field.Description: Record the failure and continue with the next step.

Field.Name: Fallback
Field.Description: Continue at FallbackStepId instead.

Field.Name: Compensate
Field.Description: Run the fallback step to undo the work already done, then end the mission.

UADataType.Description: How the transitions leaving one step relate to each other, following the divergence of an IEC 61131-3 sequential function chart.

Field.Name: Alternative
Field.Description: Exactly one transition is taken - the first whose condition holds. An OR divergence.

Field.Name: Parallel
Field.Description: Every transition is taken and the branches run concurrently. An AND divergence.

UADataType.Description: The oscillation applied across an arc weld seam.

Field.Name: None
Field.Description: No weave.

Field.Name: Sine
Field.Description: Sinusoidal oscillation.

Field.Name: Zigzag
Field.Description: Triangular oscillation.

Field.Name: Trapezoid
Field.Description: Trapezoidal oscillation, with a dwell at each edge.

UADataType.Description: One point of a time-parameterised path. Positions are per axis in the order the axes are declared, in radians or metres by AxisKind. TimeFromStart is measured from the start of the trajectory, which is what makes the path a trajectory rather than a list of waypoints. Velocities and Accelerations are optional and may be empty.

Field.Name: TimeFromStart
Field.Description: Milliseconds from the start of the trajectory.

Field.Name: Positions
Field.Description: One value per axis.

Field.Name: Velocities
Field.Description: One value per axis, or empty.

Field.Name: Accelerations
Field.Description: One value per axis, or empty.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: How far execution may deviate before it is a failure. A tolerance of zero or less means the Server applies its own.

Field.Name: Position
Field.Description: Positional tolerance in metres.

Field.Name: Orientation
Field.Description: Orientation tolerance in radians.

Field.Name: Time
Field.Description: Timing tolerance in milliseconds.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Execute a time-parameterised path. The Server's own motion kernel runs it; this interface hands the whole trajectory over in one submission and does not stream it. That is what makes trajectory execution expressible here when real-time control is not - see clause 4.3.

Field.Name: Points
Field.Description: The trajectory, in ascending TimeFromStart order.

Field.Name: PathTolerance
Field.Description: Permitted deviation while following the path.

Field.Name: GoalTolerance
Field.Description: Permitted deviation at the final point.

Field.Name: GoalTimeTolerance
Field.Description: How much later than the final point's TimeFromStart completion may be, in milliseconds.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: One waypoint of a Cartesian path, with the blend that applies at it. Per-waypoint blending is what distinguishes a path from a sequence of separate linear moves: the robot need not stop between them.

Field.Name: Pose
Field.Description: Where the tool centre point passes.

Field.Name: Blend
Field.Description: How this waypoint is left.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Follow a list of Cartesian waypoints. This is the portable form of a taught path, and unlike a trajectory it carries no timing: the Server paces it from the motion constraints.

Field.Name: Waypoints
Field.Description: The path, in order.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Move until contact. The portable subset of the force-controlled moves every vendor offers: travel along a direction until a contact force is reached or a distance is exhausted, whichever comes first. Reaching the distance without contact is a failure, because the intent was to touch something.

Field.Name: Direction
Field.Description: Unit direction of travel (x, y, z) in the frame of the target.

Field.Name: FrameId
Field.Description: The CoordinateFrame Direction is expressed in; empty for the default work frame.

Field.Name: ContactForce
Field.Description: The force in newtons at which contact is declared.

Field.Name: MaxDistance
Field.Description: How far to travel before giving up, in metres.

Field.Name: HoldForce
Field.Description: True to keep pressing at ContactForce after contact rather than stopping.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Abstract base of the intents that run an application process along a path. Every process needs the same two things beyond its own parameters: a reference to the process program or procedure the equipment holds, and room for the parameters this specification has not standardised.

Field.Name: ProcessProgram
Field.Description: The Program or equipment-side procedure to run, or null when the parameters here are sufficient.

Field.Name: Attributes
Field.Description: Further named parameters the Server declares in its capabilities.

UADataType.Description: Lay an arc weld along the path. The parameters are the subset ABB seamdata/welddata/weavedata, FANUC weld schedules and KUKA ArcTech all carry. WeldProcedureRef points at a welding procedure specification (ISO 15609) where the installation works to one; this specification does not restate its content.

Field.Name: Voltage
Field.Description: Arc voltage in volts.

Field.Name: WireFeedSpeed
Field.Description: Wire feed speed in metres per minute.

Field.Name: TravelSpeed
Field.Description: Tool centre point speed in metres per second.

Field.Name: GasPreflowTime
Field.Description: Shielding gas pre-flow, in milliseconds.

Field.Name: GasPostflowTime
Field.Description: Shielding gas post-flow, in milliseconds.

Field.Name: ArcStartDelay
Field.Description: Delay before travel begins, in milliseconds.

Field.Name: CraterFillTime
Field.Description: Crater fill at the end of the seam, in milliseconds.

Field.Name: WeaveShape
Field.Description: Oscillation across the seam.

Field.Name: WeaveAmplitude
Field.Description: Peak-to-peak weave width in metres.

Field.Name: WeaveFrequency
Field.Description: Weave frequency in hertz.

Field.Name: SeamTrackingEnabled
Field.Description: True to enable seam tracking where the equipment provides it.

Field.Name: WeldProcedureRef
Field.Description: Identifier of the welding procedure specification this weld works to.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Make a resistance spot weld at the target. WeldSchedule selects the weld controller's own program: current and time are the weld controller's business, and are carried here only where the installation drives them from the robot.

Field.Name: WeldSchedule
Field.Description: The weld controller program to run.

Field.Name: GunForce
Field.Description: Electrode force in newtons.

Field.Name: ApproachDistance
Field.Description: Gun open distance before the weld, in metres.

Field.Name: RetractDistance
Field.Description: Gun open distance after the weld, in metres.

Field.Name: MaterialThickness
Field.Description: Total stack thickness in metres, where the schedule is chosen adaptively.

Field.Name: TipDressRequested
Field.Description: True to dress the tips after this weld.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Lay a bead of adhesive, sealant or paint along the path. The trigger distances exist because material does not start and stop instantly: a Server begins dispensing before the path and stops before its end.

Field.Name: FlowRate
Field.Description: Nominal flow in millilitres per minute.

Field.Name: TriggerOnDistance
Field.Description: Distance before the path start at which dispensing begins, in metres.

Field.Name: TriggerOffDistance
Field.Description: Distance before the path end at which dispensing stops, in metres.

Field.Name: BeadWidth
Field.Description: Target bead width in metres.

Field.Name: MaterialTemperature
Field.Description: Material temperature in degrees Celsius, for hot-melt work.

Field.Name: PurgeCycles
Field.Description: Nozzle purge cycles before starting.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Drive a fastener at the target. This intent is deliberately THIN: OPC 40450 and OPC 40451 already define joining and tightening in full, so Joint references the joint in that model and the result belongs there. Restating those parameters here would create a second definition of the same fact.

Field.Name: Joint
Field.Description: The joint being fastened, in an OPC UA joining or tightening model where one is implemented.

Field.Name: ProgramNumber
Field.Description: The tightening program the tool is to run.

Field.Name: TargetTorque
Field.Description: Target torque in newton metres, where the robot supplies it rather than the tool.

Field.Name: TargetAngle
Field.Description: Target angle in radians, for angle-controlled strategies.

Field.Name: SnugTorque
Field.Description: Torque at which angle counting begins, in newton metres.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Place an item into a pattern. The pattern itself is a Location, so its geometry has one definition that a client can read rather than being recomputed from indices on both sides.

Field.Name: Pattern
Field.Description: The Location describing the pallet or pattern.

Field.Name: Layer
Field.Description: Layer index, counting from zero.

Field.Name: Row
Field.Description: Row index within the layer, counting from zero.

Field.Name: Column
Field.Description: Column index within the row, counting from zero.

Field.Name: ItemOrientation
Field.Description: Rotation of the item about the pattern normal, in radians.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: Follow the path pressing into the surface - grinding, polishing, deburring or sanding. ContactForce is what distinguishes it from a plain path: the robot yields normal to the surface to hold that force.

Field.Name: ContactForce
Field.Description: Force normal to the surface, in newtons.

Field.Name: FeedRate
Field.Description: Travel speed along the surface, in metres per second.

Field.Name: ToolSpeed
Field.Description: Rotational speed of the tool, in revolutions per minute.

Field.Name: StepOver
Field.Description: Lateral offset between adjacent passes, in metres.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: One edge of a mission's step graph, following the step-and-transition form of an IEC 61131-3 sequential function chart. Condition is an OPC UA ContentFilter - the base specification's own filter grammar, reused so that this specification does not invent an expression language for implementers to write a parser for.

Field.Name: FromStepId
Field.Description: The step this transition leaves.

Field.Name: ToStepId
Field.Description: The step this transition enters.

Field.Name: Condition
Field.Description: The condition under which it is taken. An empty filter is always true.

Field.Name: DivergenceKind
Field.Description: How this transition relates to the others leaving the same step.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UADataType.Description: One joint of the kinematic chain: where it sits relative to its predecessor and which way it acts. OPC 40010-1 describes a robot's topology and its axes but defines no kinematic chain, so this is additive rather than a second account of the same thing.

Field.Name: AxisId
Field.Description: The AxisType this joint corresponds to.

Field.Name: Kind
Field.Description: Whether it rotates or translates.

Field.Name: OriginTransform
Field.Description: Pose of this joint's frame within its predecessor's, at zero position.

Field.Name: AxisVector
Field.Description: Unit vector (x, y, z) the joint rotates about or translates along, in its own frame.

UAObject.Description: Default Binary encoding of the structure.

UAObjectType.Description: What the robot's safety system is doing, reported so a client can act sensibly around it. Every member is READ-ONLY and every one is a report: the safety system enforces these independently, remains effective when this interface is unreachable, and is not commanded from here. Clause 10 states the boundary and this type does not cross it.

UAVariable.Description: The safe motion function currently enforced, per IEC 61800-5-2.
True while an emergency stop is asserted.
True while a protective stop is asserted.
True while a safely limited speed is being enforced.
The tool centre point speed limit being enforced, in metres per second. Meaningful only while SafeSpeedLimitActive. Clause 10.3 requires a Server to refuse an intent that asks to exceed it.
False when the safety system reports its own fault. A Server accepts no intent while it is false.
Why the last stop occurred, for a human. Never parsed.

UAObjectType.Description: A high-rate channel this Server can offer, described so a client can open it. The samples never traverse OPC UA: this brokers the endpoint and nothing more, in the same way the Vision model brokers a media endpoint rather than carrying pixels. Clause 4.3 explains why the alternative is not available.

UAVariable.Description: Identifier unique within the controller.
The transport this channel speaks.
Where the channel is reached. Its scheme and form are the transport's, not this specification's.
Which end opens the connection.
The rate the channel runs at, in hertz.
The recipe, signal list or configuration the transport requires, in the transport's own form.
The operational mode the robot must be in before the channel will carry motion.
True when the channel can be opened now.
SessionId of the client currently holding the channel, or null.
When the current lease lapses. A lease that is not renewed frees the channel, so a client that dies does not hold it for good.

UAObjectType.Description: Enough of the robot's construction for a client to plan against it without a second specification: the kinematic chain, the space it can reach, and what it can carry. OPC 40010-1 describes topology and axes and defines no kinematic chain and no tool centre point, so this adds rather than restates - Annex B says which side decides where both are present.

UAVariable.Description: Who made the robot.
The robot's model designation.
The joints from the base outwards, in order.
Pose of the robot base within the world frame.
Radius of the reachable workspace from the base, in metres.
Largest payload at the mechanical interface, in kilograms.
Largest tool centre point speed the robot will produce, in metres per second.
Largest tool centre point acceleration, in metres per second squared.

UAObject.Description: What the safety system is doing. A client reads this before it plans, and subscribes to it so that it learns of a stop rather than inferring one from a refusal.
The robot's kinematics and limits.
The high-rate channels this Server can broker.

UAMethod.Description: Take a lease on a brokered real-time channel. The Server prepares the transport and returns what the client needs in order to connect; it does not carry the samples. A lease that is not renewed lapses, which is what stops a dead client from holding the channel.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The channel to open.
How long the lease is wanted for, in milliseconds.
True when the lease was taken.
Where to connect.
The transport's own configuration.
When the lease lapses.
Human-readable detail on a refusal. For a human; never parsed.

UAMethod.Description: Give up a lease on a brokered channel.

uax:Description.uax:Text: The channel to release.
True when the lease was held and is now released.

UAVariable.Description: True when trajectory and Cartesian path intents are accepted.
True when force intents are accepted and the robot can actually regulate force. A Server that would ignore the force reports false rather than accepting an intent it cannot honour.
True when the Server brokers real-time channels.
True when mission transitions are evaluated. A Server that reports false executes the steps in order and ignores any transitions supplied.
Largest number of points accepted in one trajectory. Zero means the Server states no limit.

UAObject.Description: Part 10 result container. Carries the same IntentResultDataType value as Result, so a Part 10 client finds the outcome where Part 10 says it will be. Mandatory here because clause 6.7 requires it and an Optional member cannot carry a SHALL.

UAVariable.Description: Part 10 invocation diagnostics: which Session invoked the program, when, with what arguments and to what outcome. Mandatory here because the auditable-commanding property of clause 1.2 is exactly this member, and a capability the specification advertises cannot rest on one a Server may omit. Declared exactly as OPC 10000-10 declares it - a Variable of ProgramDiagnostic2Type reached by HasComponent, with the inherited namespace-0 BrowseName - because a promotion that altered the inherited member's TypeDefinition, reference type or BrowseName namespace would declare a second member rather than promote the inherited one.

The facets of Table 12.2 this controller claims, by the names given there. A client reads this instead of re-deriving conformance from the address space. Clause 12.2 binds the claim: a facet whose structural requirements are unmet shall not appear, and the behavioural requirements are subject to the honesty rules of clause 9.
